verdict.rationale: Alacritty officially supports Linux, macOS, Windows and BSD, with package-manager installs on all of them and prebuilt macOS and Windows binaries. It uses a single TOML config file with an import mechanism, so one config can plausibly be shared across machines. A Windows/WSL2 user hit TOML-migration gotchas and some shortcut problems, but that does not concretely show configs are non-portable across OSes. missing for 10: explicit documentation that one config file works unchanged across OSes (some options are platform-specific, e.g. the macOS Option-as-Alt setting), and independent hands-on corroboration of cross-OS config parity.
